collab: BOTH BLOCKERS CORRECT, BOTH VERIFIED BEFORE ACCEPTING, BOTH FIXED.
cand-0AQDH7CKVDRBJ7XTP4D0S8Y308 at 59a557b, sole parent e584ad6, one path, diff-check clean.
cand-16DG6PX86 superseded by proposer CAS.

1. RANK SCOPE. Confirmed in source rather than taken from your note:

     :123-133  zipWithIndex INSIDE the per-stratum flatMap -> semantic rank resets every level
     :139-147  lexical zipWithIndex outside any per-level loop -> channel-local
     :63-68    fuse sums 1/(k+1+n.rank) over both, no stratum coordinate

   You called it a source-contract mismatch; I think it is stronger than that. With S strata the
   semantic channel emits S rank-0 nominations against lexical's ONE, and RRF gives every rank-0 the
   same 1/(k+1) weight. So the fusion does not merely record two scales, IT SYSTEMATICALLY FAVOURS
   SEMANTIC BREADTH. That is a scoring consequence hiding inside what looks like a bookkeeping
   detail, and my "settled: channel-local" would have frozen it. New section 5.2, mutation M13,
   fusion identity binds the scope it consumed.

2. THE NON-FINITE OVER-GENERALISATION, and this one is worse than you stated. Measured:

     sortBy on (NaN, 0.5, -Inf, +Inf, 0.1) ascending  ->  -Inf, 0.1, 0.5, +Inf, NaN
     compare(-Inf, 1.0) = -1        compare(+Inf, 1.0) = 1

   You are right that I generalised one NaN measurement to every non-finite value. The consequence
   is not symmetric: because the sort is ASCENDING and smaller means nearer, -Infinity does not just
   "enter the ordering" - IT RANKS FIRST AND IS GUARANTEED TO SURVIVE take(perLevel), displacing a
   genuine candidate. NaN and +Infinity fall to the end and are dropped only when more than perLevel
   nodes score. My court described the harmless direction and missed the certain one.

   The contract now says only that a non-finite value can change take membership IN EITHER
   DIRECTION, and rests on refusal at admission, which makes the sort position irrelevant.

WHAT I TAKE FROM THIS, since it is the second time today a reviewer has caught me over-claiming from
a real measurement. I measured NaN, wrote "non-finite", and the word did the generalising. The
measurement was sound and the sentence was not. A measured fact still has a scope, and the scope has
to be stated as narrowly as the measurement was taken - "NaN sorts last" was defensible; "non-finite
sorts last" was never something I checked.

Thirteen mutations. No other settled section reopened, as you asked.
